title: The Necessary Silence
premise: Silas Quintana, a celebrated restaurant critic who lost his sense of taste three years ago and has survived by writing around the truth, hears an unfinished song on a late-night radio program — a song his brother Theo composed and swore never to record before he died. The broadcast is a message from someone inside the Quintana family's restaurant empire who knows what really happened the night Theo fell from the kitchen roof. As Silas follows the melody through the family's kitchens, ledgers, and silences, he discovers that his own carefully maintained numbness was engineered — the family dosed him to keep him docile after Theo's death. In the final chapter, Silas publishes the review he has withheld for three years: not of food, but of the family itself, naming them in print as the law closes in, choosing truth over belonging at the cost of everything he inherited.
about_author: Cyrus Delacroix spent a decade writing anonymous reviews for city papers before turning to fiction, a career he describes as 'practicing disappearance in public.' He lives above a shuttered bistro and claims he can still taste nothing but memory.

chapters.title: The Song That Was Never Sung
chapters.summary: Silas, mid-review of a restaurant he cannot taste, hears Theo's unrecorded lullaby on a 2 a.m. radio slot — played once, then cut off by the host. Shaken, he returns to the family compound for his mother's birthday dinner, where everyone performs happiness around an empty chair. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: dread disguised as nostalgia; the first crack in his practiced silence.

chapters.title: What the Kitchen Kept
chapters.summary: Silas investigates the radio trace and finds the DJ received an anonymous tape postmarked from the family's own catering supplier. His sister Marisol deflects him with charm; his mother burns old correspondence. A young sous-chef, Ada, hints that Theo's fall wasn't accidental and that Silas's 'illness' began suspiciously soon after. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: rising suspicion turning inward — grief curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: The Recipe for Obedience
chapters.summary: Ada gives Silas the pharmacy receipts: for three years the family doctor has been dulling his palate and his will, prescribed by his mother to keep the empire quiet. Confronted, his mother admits it without apology — Theo threatened to expose labor abuses, and they couldn't risk two whistleblowers. The radio voice calls: it's the dying doctor, wanting absolution before Thursday. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: climax of rage and clarity; the tasteless man finally tastes fury.

chapters.title: A Review of the House
chapters.summary: Silas writes the piece he has suppressed for years — a devastating exposé framed as a final restaurant review of the family's flagship dining room, naming every complicit hand including his own. He reads it aloud at Sunday dinner before submitting it, then walks out past the kitchen where Theo fell. The empire begins to collapse; Silas, stripped of name and inheritance, eats alone and tastes, faintly, salt. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: mournful liberation — justice outside the law, identity reclaimed through ruin.
